I will keep my farm in the standard Quzhou grain pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am in southern Hebei on the North China Plain, where this rotation is still the dominant and most stable system, and recent Quzhou “吨半粮” work shows the county can push wheat plus maize yields very high with tighter water-fertilizer management. At 68, even with strong education, I would not spread myself across labor-heavy vegetables or uncertain cash crops. I want a system I can mechanize, manage carefully, and finish on time. I will assume I am managing 20 mu of arable land and put all 20 mu into the wheat-maize rotation. For wheat, I will use an improved local winter wheat variety, keep fertilizer in the moderate-high range instead of chasing yield with excess nitrogen, irrigate three times because wheat season is dry here, and use rotary tillage after maize residue incorporation. For summer maize, I will switch to hybrid seed, use one-pass precise sowing after wheat harvest with no-tillage to save time and moisture, keep fertilizer balanced, irrigate only once unless drought forces more, and limit pesticide sprays to what is needed for weeds and major insects and diseases. My goal is steady grain output, manageable labor, and lower waste rather than maximum-input farming.
